utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everybody in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, The Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Kyle Wood for the Prosecution assisted by Alma Imamovic-Ivanov, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much and for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, good afternoon colleagues from the Prosecution and everyone in and around the courtroom. I am ray Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson, Defence counsel for General Rasim Delic, with our case manager, Ms. Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hubo, good afternoon. Just to remind you that you made a declaration at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth the whole truth and nothing else but the truth. You are still bound by that declaration. Okay. Thank you very much. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hubo. On Friday afternoon, Mr. Hubo, you were explaining to us problems in obtaining information from the El Mujahedin Detachment, and in that connection, I would like to show you a series of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could document D967, please be brought up on the screen. Your Honour, I see that this copy on the screen is rather poor, I wonder if I may be permitted to give a hard copy to Mr. Hubo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sort it out with your opposite number, if they are agreed. If they have seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same document that we see on the screen. Oh you just want to show a hard copy to make sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: No, objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for the record what we can see here is a document with the heading, rules on keeping records of registration and deregistration of place of residence for foreigners who are members of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina armed forces in times of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, have you -- are you familiar with this document at all?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This document did circulate in the course of our work and it referred to, as you can see, actually it was the rules on keeping recording of registration and the deregistration of place of residence for foreigners who are members of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina armed forces in times of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date that these rules were issued?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These rules were issued on 23rd June 1994, and signer is the Minister of Defence and Minister of Interior of Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But the time when it actually was published was 13 June 1994, and it was published on the 23rd of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know -- were these rules in force?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the translation says by the time when it actually was published was the 13th June 1994 and it was published on the 23rd of June, 1994. That is one and the same thing. Was it printed on the 13th and published on the 24th, or what is the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, perhaps you could just repeat the last part of your answer and just explain when the document was -- was issued?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was signed on 13 June 1994, probably at the session of the government, and it was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the -- on the 23rd of June, 1994. So at the time when it was published, it actually came into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at Article 12 it says: "These rules stipulate the ways in which records are kept of the registration and deregistration of the place of residence of foreigners who are members of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina armed forces." Now, last week we spoke about foreigners that joined the El Mujahedin detachment. Do you know, should these rules have applied to those foreigners who joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These rules applied to all foreigners, members of the armed forces. And so let me just clarify, it also applied to the foreigners within the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we look at Article 2, what it says is: "The foreigner under Article 1 of these rules or the commander of the unit or institution to which the foreigner belongs shall submit within seven days of joining a unit a registration of residence form for the foreigner to the Municipal Secretariat for National Defence in the area in which the foreigner is staying ..." Mr. Hubo, do you know what this reference to a registration of residence form means? What was it that was supposed to be supplied to the Municipal Defence Secretariat?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: These rules defined the manner in which every foreigner is to register, his place of residence, because the normal procedure was when a foreigner would enter a country, the registration of his stay in the country would have -- should be with the Ministry of Interior. I suppose that in this particular case and in many cases such a form did not exist once a person joined a unit of the armed force, there was -- here this provides for the possibility for a subsequent report or registration by the command of the unit at the time when this foreigner joined the armed forces. So in any case, this registration should be available to the Ministry of the Defence and of course for all those foreigners who were with -- within the unit, and here, in particular, it speaks of the municipality in which that unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So a registration form should have been provided to the Municipal Defence Secretariat. Are you aware following June of 1994 any situation in which the El Mujahedin Detachment passed such information to the Municipal Defence Secretariat in compliance with these rules?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to information that I received from the Secretariat for Defence, this was never done by the detachment as a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I move to admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need a clarification on this document, please. Witness, please, the commander that is mentioned under Article 2, and he is mentioned in the three paragraphs of Article 2, is he supposed to be the commander of a regular unit of the army, or can it -- could he also be the commander of a volunteer unit, which is exactly the case of the El Mujahedin Detachment. I don't quite understand this. Could you please read the -- read Article 2 and maybe enlighten me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as you can observe, in the last paragraph of Article 2, and I'm not a legal lawyer, but there were lawyers working in my office and in the Secretariat for Defence you will see that it says here: "The commander of the unit, under Article 1, Article 2 in this case, shall be the senior officer in the position of commander of an independent battalion or above." In other words, all commanders at this level and in particular in this -- in the case of this unit, that's what it referred to, they were -- this provision also referred to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So this third paragraph could also make reference to the commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment, this commander of the unit could very well be the commander of El Mujahedin Detachment detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I know it frequently happens that you have things stated in the laws that are not really performed in practice. Now, the existence of the El Mujahid Detachment was well-known. These rules came about and they were also well known, and now you tell us that no member of the El Mujahid Detachment ever registered as he should have done, according to these rules. What did you do about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that respect, we compiled a so-called data base for every unit and we tried, we received for, in a certain period of time we received some information. When I say "some," it means that we received them as they were forwarded by the unit from the corps command. All this information that we received from this unit we forwarded on to the secretariats, the centre for security services and other organs. So everything that we came into possession as the command, we informed of all the relevant institutions. But I have to say right here that the information that we obtained did not meet all the contents that were provided for by these rules, and other regulations. In other words, what we had under our control, we did, and you're absolutely right when you speak of the compliance with legal provisions, but I'm telling you about the -- the procedures that we used as we used, and of course we were obliged by the law to act within that scope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So, after all, did you get some information about the El Mujahid Detachment. Could you tell us what that information was, and how it was provided, by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm glad that you've asked this question. In the second phases or latter phases of the organisation of the corps, we used electronic media. So we looked for additional auxiliary information. We refer to this as a data base. This database consisted of a list of all members of the corps. This is 35 and 40.000 people. This database was done by the subordinate units and we used this as auxiliary documentation so that we can control the personnel better and direct them better. At one point, this information on a floppy disk as I mentioned earlier that individual who could come from the unit so from time to time he would bring the floppy disk. The information was as it was compiled within the unit in all its aspects: The contents, the form, and all other aspects. This is all that we could obtain. All the information that we had, I have to stress again, we forwarded to other institutions as provided for by the law and within the capabilities that we had. So this was an attempt on our part to obtain as much information as we could so that we could comply with all these requirements that were -- all the requirements that were set forth in the different legal documents. If you ask me whether that was enough, it certainly wasn't either in form or in content, substance, up until the end of when this unit was actually disbanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm still not sure that I understood what the information was that you actually did get on these floppy disks and who was it that gave the disk to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information consisted of the following: The name and last name, date and place of birth, military speciality or VES for short, the date of entry into the army, completed education, level of education, high school or university, and a host of other personal data that we had within the corps command for each member, so that we were able to, when asked to provide an officer who was an engineer, we would use this database to submit a request for this profile and then the programme would automatically give us a list of all engineers that we had within the corps. We call this a database for each member of the army because we also had situations where family member would inquire about their relative. Whether there were alive or not, and we would use this to find out that information. Whether that person was still there, whether -- in what unit and what kind of status.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I think we are misunderstanding each other. It seems to me that you have been telling me how the system worked in general. The information that I was asking you about, was whether you received any general information about the members of the El Mujahid Detachment and was that fed into your database, because I understood you to say just a while ago that after all you did, in fact, get some information about the El Mujahid Detachment, and I'm curious to know what was that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information was provided to us in a period of time from this unit, with some information, information that were -- that was collected within the unit itself, and there are instances where we have listed of all the members of the unit. This was provided by the unit itself with the name and last name and where the person was from, when they joined the army, when they completed or left the army, so it was provided by the unit. And at one point they were forwarded into electronic form, and this base from this unit is what we used so that we could further do the part of work that was within our jurisdiction. I don't know if I was clear in my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You were perfectly clear and maybe we did not misunderstand each other or I did not misunderstand you when you spoke to us just a while ago, because all the information that you mentioned in your first answer to me, the name and the last name of the member, the date and place of birth, the military specialty, the date of entry into the army, the complete education, the level of education, the high school and university, was that information that you received also from the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received some information, and this information was, as it were, not in proper form, and more often than not it was useless. It was impossible to use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In what sense "useless"? Because it would seem to be to be quite comprehensive information at least about some of the members of the El Mujahid Detachment, including the previous education that these gentlemen had.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well I'll give you an example. For instance, you have information where each name begins with Abu on a list of names it's impossible that the hundred-or-so people are all called Abu. It is possible that there is no information on which country they came from and so forth. So all of this actually to us meant that this information was incorrect, and we couldn't uses it as official data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The other question I had was who gave the disk to you? Was that a member of the El Mujahid Detachment who came by your office and handed over the disk to you, or how did you get it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned earlier, I believe on Friday, that there was an individual who came to us. His name was Muris Supic and this person, in fact, was the only individual who communicated with us. He came whenever he chose and brought whatever he chose, as it were, and that's when they forwarded this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1312.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, just to pick up on a point from Judge Harhoff's questions. Within the information that was provided to your organ, did the El Mujahedin Detachment ever provide information such as passports numbers or identification numbers for any of the members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, that's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I disagree. I can certainly rephrase it though. If that may be to no avail now that I have raised the question with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you think you can rephrase, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Let me, first of all, clarify another point. It was unclear to me whether the El Mujahedin Detachment provided information about the previous experience of its members or not. Could you tell me what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't quite clear, but I told the honourable Judge a few minutes ago, even the information, this database that we received, we didn't even receive information as to which country this individual -- any individual came from let alone passport numbers and so on. And we absolutely had no other information but those that were forwarded by them, as far as the organ in which I worked was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to bring up a document at this stage. It is Exhibit 663.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, this document is several pages long in the B/C/S version. First of all, if I could just ask to you take a look at the top half of the page. Do you recognise the document at all?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this document. It has a number, and the heading, has a date, so -- and this document is in the form that the corps produced, the documents that the corps produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we could just go to the last page in the B/C/S version. We see a name there. Do you know who was the author of this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was prepared by a person who worked on the issue of registration of individual conscript, and EH I think this could have been Emir Hurem. E/H, that means that this same person prepared the document and also printed it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And we can see that the document bears your name, is that right, it was sent out in your name?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the usual form in which the document would appear. My signature is not there, but it could have been there. So if someone officially requested, we had the obligation to provide the information that we had available. In this particular case, the military security service probably requested this information, and they probably did security checks for whatever reasons, this was not something that we would go into but what we had in our database we made a copy of and forwarded it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can go back to the first page in the B/C/S, so that we can touch upon what you just mentioned. We can see there that this -- well, can you tell us who was this document sent to?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was produced by the 3rd Corps command, the confidential number is 05/4. 05 means that it is the organ for mobilisation and personnel affairs. Then it says Zenica 7th of May, 1995. The subject is a list which was sent to the military security service department of the 3rd Corps command. It says on your request. This means that there was an ongoing activity with the aim of obtaining reliable information and this was done by the military security service in cooperation with the Ministry of Defence because we were trying all the time to obtain reliable information about the individuals. As can you see also on the basis of this list, it is very hard to get accurate information. You can see that there is information missing, if you look at the contents of the document, which you can also see and this is something that I said to His Honour, the Judge. There's a list of names saying Abu countless times. As to the place and date of birth in the third column there's the information there for some individuals, for some it is missing, and there's a number of deficiencies an information missing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. So this document was produced within the 3rd Corps. Do you know what the source of the information was for this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sole source of information in all of the other documents that were made are out of this was the disk and whatever the El Mujahid Detachment delivered to the 3rd Corps. All the other documents were produced on the basis of this database that was compiled in the unit. We had no other possibilities of dealing with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And was there any -- do you know, was the information verified once it was received on the floppy disk before this list was produced?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean whether we double-checked the information?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't able to do that. We were complaining about this and as a result probably the military security service which had tried dealing with the other state organs of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to make double-checks in its own right, we, as the command, tried to track down some information that we were interested in and that we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I'm told that during your answer you mentioned the MUP, the Ministry of Interior and that has not been captured in the transcript. Did you mention that at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. That is essentially a leading question. If there's a problem with the transcript, the Defence counsel can say can you please repeat your last answer. When he says something was mentioned that didn't appear in the transcript that is a way that he can suggest the answer or suggest or guide the testimony of the witness. I would suggest, Your Honour, that the best way to do that so as to avoid any kind of leading question is to say, Can you please repeat your last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my only concern with that approach is that the -- often the witness's answers are fairly lengthy and we have had a few situations now where I have asked the witness to respond and it has been a fairly complicated approach. I have certainly no problem in asking the witness to repeats the answer if that is what the Bench would like. As to the suggestion that we could somehow lead the witness, Your Honours, clearly, the proceedings are videotaped. There are capture -- there would be ways to see whether or not we were suggesting that the witness -- we were putting to the witness that he should perhaps move to the issue of the MUP, so I was really just trying to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's try to observe the rules before we try to save time. Could you ask the witness to repeat himself, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I don't know if you can remember my last question. Are you able to repeat for us what you told us a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't repeat it in the form I used initially, but I can give you the gist. This list was send to the military security service department of the corps command, probably with a view to carrying out checks and verifying some information. The military security service operated professionally with the organs of the Ministry of Interior, just as the organ for personnel also cooperated with the organs professionally with the military security. You had organs of the army, the professional organs, which in their own line of activity cooperated with respective state organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thanks. Your Honours, we can put this document away, and I'd like to turn to another one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just find out one little point. Mr. Hubo, is it your testimony that this kind of list would be the kind of list that would have been generated in compliance with Exhibit 1312, that is the document that we saw a little earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid I didn't quite understand your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we were shown this document, we were shown another document which was entitled "Rules on the Registration of Residents of Foreign Fighters." Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have a copy of it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. My question is: Is this list being generated and supplied in compliance with that document, with those rules, or are these two completely unrelated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this specific case one has nothing to do with the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Exhibit 110, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, can you tell us what you see on the screen in front of you? Are you able to make it out?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see here an order by the corps commander, a document which was made. I can't see the date clearly. The 8th of May, 1995. And which has to do with the update of personal information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Is this order signed?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that it is signed. And it is quite unusual that it does not bear a date in item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Hmm. And can we see who was this document sent to -- or, sorry. Let me ask that again. At the bottom of the page we can see that if the document was to be sent, which unit should it have gone to?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says delivered to the El Mujahid Detachment and files.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In point number 1 of this order what it states is: "For members of the ARBiH foreign nationals submit information on personnel file which is a supplement to this document to the corps command department for organisation mobilisation and personnel affairs." First of all, is that your organ that this information should have been sent to?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the organ I was heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And where this document refers to submit information on personnel file which is a supplement to this document, what would you expect to find together with this document, this order?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course every supplement or annex is always a part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you describe for us what you say the annex or supplement would have looked like or should have looked like?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a form which was called, I suppose PERS 7, which was customary form, which all the commands should have received from the Municipal Defence Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. So just so I'm clear, you would have expected to find an example of such a form with this document. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Not only is that a leading question in that the form of it suggests the answer, but it is also cumulative. It's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is also?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Cumulative, Your Honour. It's been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, first of all, Your Honour, the witness gave his last answer, so I'm simply building upon what he told us. It is -- my question was certainly just to ascertain with clarity what he meant by his last answer, and I don't believe it was cumulative, it was just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I suppose strictly speaking in form it is leading, but I can understand you are building. Perhaps if it had been put like how that form was delivered or how it was sent, if indeed it makes a problem to suggest that it is sent together with a previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I think the answer is clear enough, looking at it once again. So I'm going to move to a different question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe before you move to a different question, I'd like to ask a question to the witness as a follow-up to the question I asked a couple of minutes ago. Mr. Hubo, was there ever a list drawn up of foreign fighters in compliance with Exhibit 1312? Exhibit 1312 being the document that you have in front of you there in hard copy, registration of residence of foreign fighters. I'm asking you this question because you're saying to me -- you said a little earlier that the list that was now on the screen has nothing to do with that document when I asked you whether it was drawn in compliance, you said no. And my question was to you is, was there ever a list generated in compliance with those rules.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I told you that I didn't know whether that particular document was produced in compliance with the document I have here before me. The only list that they did produce was the one that we saw. Now as to whether they compiled the list in accordance with the document I have here, that unit should have sent it to the Municipal Defence Secretariat, that particular list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You did not say you don't know when you answered my question. I'll refer you to page 16, lines 11 and 12. Let me start at line 8 where my question is. I said that's right my question is this list being generated and supplied in compliance with that document with those rules or are these two completely unrelated? Your answer was: "In this specific case one was nothing to do with the other." You didn't say I don't know. And it is because of this answer that I'm asking you this follow-up question. I want to know if these two documents have nothing to do with each other, was there ever a list generated in compliance with those rules? And the second reason I'm asking you this question is because those rules call specifically for residential particulars, and this list doesn't give residential particulars, nor does it provide for a column for residential particulars.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this information was not compiled pursuant to that document that I have here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. You have told me that before. Now my question is: Was there ever a list generated pursuant to those rules; in other words, did your department comply with those rules and ask from the members the information that those rules is asking for, or was it just a law that was made and was never observed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The role of our organ was not to make that list itself. The units were supposed to draw up the lists and send them to the secretariat. We were not making the lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear you, sir. I understand you. Do you know whether those lists were ever made? Were they made by the units or by whoever? Do you know whether they were ever made in compliance with those rules?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, I want to take you back to the last answer that you gave me a few minutes ago. You said that concerning this order, this unsigned order, you were you would have expected there to be an annex, and in the annex there should have been a form which you said was called, you suppose, PERS 7. I'd now like to look at the next page in the B/C/S version, and we can also look at the next page in English to see what was actually together with this document. Is this the form PERS 7 that should have been with the order or you would have expected with the order?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not a form of any sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And the information that we see on the page in front of us, have you ever seen this -- this list before?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether I saw these lists or not, but they are lists just as many others. Probably this list was made in the unit. You can see that by the font and all the hallmarks of the document. It was copied, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you say it was -- when you say probably this list was made in the unit, which unit are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, throughout the time -- all the time I meant the El Mujahedin Detachment as the specific unit, the peculiar unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just going back to the first page again, please, and the document we see there. You told us that the document was from May 1995. Do you know, was there an attempt to get the El Mujahedin Detachment to submit information on a personal [Realtime transcript read in error "personnel"] file to your organ?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever we had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Robson. Did you say personnel file or personal file?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Personal file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The transcript says personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. It has been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you give us your answer, please, Mr. Hubo.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information we received was received in the electronic form we had occasion to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And just to go back to my question, what I was asking you was whether you were aware of any attempt by the 3rd Corps to get the El Mujahedin Detachment to submit information set down in a personal file to your organ.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the time there were attempts, not only on the part of my organ but on the part of the other commands as well, to obtain information from them. I said that countless times now. And this was the case throughout the time, through to the end of the war, and we weren't able to get anything more than what we had in fact received from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. Turning, then, to some of the attempts, the other attempts that you made to obtain information, could I please bring up document D997. Mr. Hubo, we have in front of us a document dated 2nd of June, 1995. If we can just go to the second page in the English document and if we can look at the bottom of the B/C/S. Could you tell us who this order is from?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order comes from the commander of the 3rd Corps, and derives from the document of the General Staff of the army of the BH dated the 25th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could we go back to the first page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we look at point 1 in the order, it say states: "Form a commission for the reconstruction and definition of the period of service in the ARBiH for 1992 in the units for which there are no appropriate records." And then if we look at point number 4 we can see it says: "I hereby appointed the following members of the commission," and we see a list of names there. Do you recognise any of the names on that list?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them all, all the individuals listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The first name on the list is Senior Lieutenant Mustafa Spahic and we can see that he works for the section for mobilisation and personnel affairs. Is that the same organ that you worked for?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This individual belonged to the organ I worked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: The document refers to the formation of a commission. Do you have any knowledge of -- of whether a commission was actually formed in June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission was definitely set up, and it had a mixed composition, as it were. You can see in item 4 in the third column that the individuals from all the other departments of the corps were involved. The legal affairs department, the military security service department, head of office and typist, or rather the person who typed out these documents and they had time-limit of one month to -- I mean, all these persons who were nominated into this commission had one-month deadline to determine and establish the information sought herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if you are able, can you explain for us what the role of the commission was?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The role of the commission was to establish the length of service in 1992 of the members of the BiH army, in respect of the individuals who -- for whom such records do not exist. So this addresses the units who did not keep records properly but in doing so they had to comply with the law with the provisions of the Law on Administrative Procedure, whilst using all the individuals and organs that were placed at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us during your evidence that, as far as you were aware, the El Mujahedin Detachment did not keep records. Do you know whether this commission looked into the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer. I know that at a later stage had the commission done its job, we -- the -- we would have had a much clearer situation. So evidently the commission did not complete its job, and I don't know if they sent a report or who they sent a report to, and that report should have contained all the particulars about their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, there's translation issue. Could you please repeat your last answer for us once again. If you recall, my question was: Do you remember whether there commission looked into the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was duty-bound to deal with all the cases as provided for by the order. I am not familiar with the report that they should have compiled as per item 6, which they should have sent to the corps commander. However, based on the documentation and the later confrontation with the same problem, evidently this commission did not do its job properly. It had not been done the way it should have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: This document could be put away and if we could please bring up -- oh, Your Honour, please could it be admitted into evidence before it disappears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please have exhibit 1138.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Hubo, the quality of this copy on your screen is not particularly good. But are you able to make out what it says?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless my learned friend opposes, I suggest that the witness has a hard copy again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hubo, we can see here a document dated 27th of October, 1995. With the heading instruction on the engagement and records to be kept of foreign citizens in the BH army and it is from the 3rd Corps commander, General Mahmuljin. Are you familiar with this document as all?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And can you explain what it is that General Mahmuljin is trying to do by way of this document?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is dated 27th October, 1995. This is a new attempt to draw attention and insist on the uncompliance with the provisions of the laws and other documents, which prescribe the manner and method of treating foreigners who were engaged in the army units. And, again, mention is made of foreigners who were in the units from earlier on, that they should provide a statement, stating that they were voluntarily joining the unit. Since this hadn't been done in the appropriate manner, there were attempts to have all these statements provided to -- forwarded to the corps command so that the corps command could carry out this duty in place of the units by the date as stated here by the deadline of 15 November 1995. Those units who do not provide the statements will not be issued by -- will not be issued statements by this command or certificates by this command as to the movement of personnel. Any movement of personnel or new personnel joining in or leaving a unit have to be reported within 24 hours to this command, so, in other words, this is another attempt to try and excerpt some pressure on units to comply with all the provisions so not only the units but also their commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we're clear, if we look at point number 4, who should the statements have been delivered to within the corps command?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 4 it says each foreign citizen shall -- or statements given by each foreign citizen shall be delivered to the corps command to the mobilisation and personnel department by 15 November 1995 at the latest. So this is the -- a deadline of some 15 days or so, so that this job can be completed, documentation compiled and files created and forwarded to the Secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So it should have been forwarded to your organ. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know, after the 27th of August [sic], 1995, did your organ ever receive any statements relating to foreign members of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen such statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, is it after the 27th of August, or of October?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: October, Your Honour, I believe I said October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The transcript says August, just to make sure the transcript is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If the transcript could be corrected so that it is the 27th of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And the final point on this document, Mr. Hubo, if we look at the bottom of the document and if we can go to the second page in English, was this order, does it appear to be the case that this document was sent to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here delivered to. It probably means forwarded to. And it says in the bottom left part of the document whom this should be delivered to, and I suppose it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do we see the name El Mujahedin Detachment there on the list?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do. We can see in the second column.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document can be put away now. And if I could bring up another one. It's Defence document D1026.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, are you able to make out what this document dated the 13th of November, 1995 says? Is it legible on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's legible. This is an order from the corps commander, which was prepared by the organ that I headed. As we can see from the top left corner where it says confidential number 05, this is the organ. The document is dated 13 November 1995, and the subject is examining an updating files of establishment of units, order. It says here that this order shall regulate the following: On 14 November 1995 analyse the establishment of the El Mujahid Detachment unit. The task mentioned in item 1 of this order shall be carried out by the following officers, and then it lists them: Captain Senad Tahto, on behalf of the military security service; Senior Lieutenant-Colonel Mustafa Spahic, on behalf of the organization, mobilization, and personnel affairs; Senior Lieutenant Senad Mesic, on behalf of the legal affairs department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And were you aware of the 3rd Corps commander ordering the creation of this team of officers in November 1995 to analyse the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was clear. This order arose from the need to compile this information and update it. So a committee or a commission was formed, a mixed commission and the purpose, their objective was to carry out this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge of whether or not the commission was able to carry out its task?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think from the witness's last answer it's clear that he was aware of this commission being formed. He was the assistant commander of the section, and the question I put was phrased in such a way to give the witness the possibility of declining knowledge, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, do you remember the question? Are you able to answer it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No commission ever managed to carry out the task as it was expected and as it was supposed to be carried out. That is the gist of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If this is an appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson. Mr. Robson, how much longer are you still going to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will try and finish within 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, moving to a new issue, you told us that you did receive some information from the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you know at any time was there ever any attempt to control membership of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered a number of times the same question. There were ongoing attempts, up until the end of the war, but, unfortunately, that's all that they remained, attempts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could I show the witness document -- I beg your pardon. Show the witness Exhibit 591.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, this is a document dated the 22nd of April, 1995, from the 3rd Corps security department. Could you tell us who this document is addressed to? If you are unable to read this document, please let me know and we can provide with you a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document dated 22nd April 1995, sent to the department of security -- from the department of military security, to the department for legal and personnel affairs, to the attention of the assistant commander. This document was also forwarded to other services, the service the military security of the 3rd Corps, the counterintelligence department, and to the organs of the military security of the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph of the document it says: "Upon the order of the 3rd corps commander, staffing of the El Mujahedin unit was limited and further admittance of fighters was suspended, both from abroad and our citizens." Before I ask you my question, did you receive this document in April 1995 that's addressed to you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And are you able to comment at all on that first paragraph which refers to staffing of the El Mujahedin Detachment being limited and further admittance of fighters being suspended?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point, it was realised that the unit was filled up to the manning levels that were actually foreseen by the formation units, and the corps commander issued a decision to prohibit further reassignment of these -- of these soldiers to El Mujahid detachment. In order for this order to be complied with and carried out, the military security service was also involved in this operation to supervise the compliance with this order, and probably they also could apply some sanctions for all those -- to all those who did not comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know, did the El Mujahedin Detachment comply with the direction to then suspend further admittance of fighters into the unit?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, they continually forwarded requests, trying -- he continually forwarded requests trying to actually circumvent this order. But in legal and formal terms the corps command no longer reassigned men and personnel from other formations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Robson. I just want to ask for clarification. Who is the "he" referred to in this answer, Mr. Hubo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps if you can remind me of the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Could you tell us who or what continually forwarded requests to try and circumvent the order that we see in front of us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an it, it's the detachment command. When I say "he" or "it," I mean the detachment. I apologise if I omit to mentioned the name. I just want to make it clear that most often I refer to that unit, the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document can be put away. If we could please bring up Exhibit 590.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, are you able to make out what is on the screen in front of you? Again, the quality of this document is not particularly good.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The point of this document, in fact what it consists of is an order of the corps commander of 9 August 1995, ordering that the persons mentioned in the order immediately be returned to the 328th Mountain Brigade, and this order came as a result of information that the military security service provided, because can you see in the heading where it says pursuant to report from the military security service, and for the purpose of consistent implementation so they attempted in this manner, too, to provide that the order of the corps command be complied with. So these fighters, probably like the others, left their units on their own and the military security service was aware of this, and they demanded that these men not be admitted into the El Mujahid Detachment but return to their original unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can just scroll down the page in English, and -- and if we can go into the second page in English. We can see that the document bears the name Sakib Mahmuljin. Mr. Hubo, do you know whether the El Mujahedin Detachment complied with this order of the 9th of August, 1995 and returned the listed men to the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you if I know or not. It was his duty to comply with in order and to report on it, to submit a report. And from what you can see in the left bottom corner of the document where this was or whom this was forwarded to, the department of military security of the 3rd Corps command, it's obvious that the military security also had to actually monitor this, because we did not receive such reports, and there was a desire to obtain them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just to clarify one point. You said it was his duty to comply with the order. Who were you speaking of when you said it was his duty?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to be brief so that we can understand what's -- and avoid using he or it. So if you look at item 3 it says the commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment is responsible for the execution of this order and shall inform this command in writing by 1500 hours on 10 August 1995 at the latest. So this is an urgent order if you look at the date there, of 9 August 1995, so the order should be complied with immediately by the commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document can be put away and if we can please bring up Exhibit 1167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, would you kindly elicit from the witness, and I'll leave it to you to put the questions if that's preferable, elicit from the witness some more information about the authority of the 3rd Corps commander to actually assign people to the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just about to move to that specific point and you see from the document when it comes up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you're going to move to that point, may -- can I clear something with the witness based on the exhibits that have been put to him so far?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, do you know whether the 3rd Corps or any authority within the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did do anything to enforce compliance with these many orders that we have been seeing sent to the El Mujahedin Detachment and with which the El Mujahedin Detachment did not comply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is difficult to answer your question. I could tell you about the procedures with others, but in this particular case, I cannot really give you an answer; but certainly the organs of the military security service were focussed on this, and it was their responsibility to inform the commander and it -- of what measures they were bringing. So I cannot really answer your question as to how it was actually was and whether it was. But in this particular case, we did not have the appropriate measures to enforce compliance. In other words, this is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to repeat the last part of the sentence. Just the last few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are requested to repeat the last part of the sentence. The interpreter didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So through my office and the orders that I had access to, I did not have the feeling that anything was accomplished in this area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your answer has given some explanation which gave me the impression we were not on the same page. Part of it says you did hear what I'm saying. But let me just repeat myself so that we have a clear understanding. We have seen a number of orders being sent to the El Mujahid Detachment to do certain things. Every one, without exception they have not complied. Did the authorities of the army use the disciplinary measures within the laws of -- of the army to ensure compliance? Are you aware of this having been done at any stage? Now I'm asking whether you are aware of it, so your answer is going to be yes, I am aware; or no, I'm not aware. And if you are aware, you will say, these are the measures that were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that -- well, the body instituting such criminal reports or measures was the military security service. I am not aware of what they were doing within the corps command, if anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Exhibit 1167, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hubo, a moment ago we previously saw a document dated the 9th of August, 1995, in which the 3rd Corps commander was ordering men to be returned from the El Mujahedin Detachment to the 328th Mountain Brigade. If I could ask you about this document in front of us, dated the 16th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, first of all, perhaps we can go to page 2 so we can clarify who the order is from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: This also is from the 3rd Corps commander. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the order of the 3rd Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if we can go to point number 1 in the order. Can you explain what the 3rd Corps commander is ordering?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In item 1 of the order the 3rd Corps commander orders that Kozlic Himze Nermin, who had so far had the position in the third large PVO should be assigned provisionally. That's the provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And where is he being assigned to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can see a little more of the English so that we know this person that is being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So we can see the persons being assigned to the El Mujahedin Detachment. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to explain what is happening with this order, why -- perhaps could you explain why the person is being assigned to the El Mujahedin Detachment, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reasons behind his assignment were, and of what nature they were. However, in the preamble, what you don't have here but can you see on page 1 of the English version - can you turn to page 1 perhaps of the English version - in the Bosnian version it says in the preamble, pursuant to Article 43, paragraph 1 of the decree law on compulsory military service, and then all the relevant legislation is listed as well as the Presidency decisions and the last part of the paragraph says: "Pursuant to the proposal of the El Mujahid Detachment command, number and dated." So it was that detachment that proposed the reassignment of the individual and 3rd Corps carried out the reassignment. I don't know what the reasons behind the reassignment were, but probably the documents state something about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. You don't know the reason for the reassignment. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't whether I can usefully explore that issue any further with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know what it is that you want to explore, Mr. Robson. It is up to you. You decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm referring to the question raised by His Honour Judge Harhoff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: -- when he wished to ask the witness about the assignment of people to the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm just unsure and I will just leave it to you if you think that this is anything that should be explored. But I'm unsure -- I'm unsure it about the significance of the correspondence of the relation between General Mahmuljin of the 3rd Corps on the one side and the El Mujahid Detachment on the other side and that's why I asked the question. But I will leave it to you to see if you want to take it any further. I mean, to me it does suggest some sort of a will to establish something that might look like subordination or at least cooperation, but I leave it to you, as I said, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, you've left me the discretion, so I'm going to move on and I'm going to deal with my final topic today; and I hope I can deal with this quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, just to take you back to the initial part of your evidence when you talked about the Municipal Defence Secretariat and you explained that the Municipal Defence Secretariat was responsible for replenishment of men in army units. Did you know, did the Municipal Defence Secretariat have any other role apart from dealing with replenishment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically speaking about the army, the secretariat also had the obligation to requisition materiel and technical equipment for the needs of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know, was there any law or regulation that governed the requisition of materiel for the needs of the army?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the preamble of the decree 19/92, the decree on the criteria and norms of the assignment of men and materiel, provides for the obligations that the secretariat had vis-a-vis the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Okay. So the decree you mentioned, that's the document that we've already looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So could I please bring up Exhibit 1310.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hubo, this is document that we looked at on Friday during your testimony. Could we please look at Article 59, which is at page 16 of the English version. And it's page 12 in the B/C/S. If you could just look at the first part of Article 59. Are you able to comment on what this provides?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 59 speaks of the takeover of resources from their owners for the needs of the users in the context of the armed forces or the MUP shall be carried out through the municipal secretariat. In other words, the secretariat is responsible for the requisitioning of assets from their owners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And if you know, can you help us, what was the procedure by which the Municipal Defence Secretariat would requisition assets and provide it to a user?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the procedure in accordance with the instant Article, the user of the assets, in other words, the unit which needed to requisition some resources would submit a written application for the requisitioning of a given asset and address it to the secretariat. As a follow-up, the secretariat examined the situation and the possibilities and where it was realistically possible, the secretariat requisitioned the relevant items from the owner, and handed the requisitioned goods on to the requesting unit, along with the relevant minutes and all the underlying documentation. In any case the secretariat was the mediator between the owner of the assets and the user of the assets, in this particular context, the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in terms of the resources which was covered by this decree, what sort of things were included within that term?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It included facilities, vehicles, all the equipment used by the armed forces, from computers to office premises, et cetera. The army had a wide range of needs. There was no other way of procuring these goods other than through this procedure, and this is the way the armed forces procured their materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you say facilities, can you be a little clearer? What do you mean by "facilities"?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant buildings, premises, necessary for the stationing of the command and the billeting of men, above all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: So you've said the Municipal Defence Secretariat was responsible for assigning these resources to military units. Once the resources were assigned to a unit, was there any type of continuing duty to oversee the use of the resources?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence, in this case its Defence Secretariat, had the possibility to constantly assess whether the resources were used as had been primarily intended, and this was one of the duties of the secretariat to examine the actual possibilities and possible uses to which the resources could be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if I could bring up my final document. It's D999.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, are you able to explain to us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a record on the inspection of utilisation of facilities appropriated for the purposes of the military unit 5689, Zenica, which is the El Mujahid Detachment. A commission was set up comprising the representatives of the district Defence Secretariat, the ministry's department in Zenica, which means the municipal officer there, and the representative of the military unit 5689. It was established here that the commission had conducted a field inspection and found that the appropriated or requisitioned facilities of Vatrostalna and Apatinska Pivara were being properly utilized, and it is also stated that the facilities were socially owned. The note reads that the Apatinska Pivara was not requisitioned due to an error, so a subsequent requested submitted for it to be appropriated and that this was a pending issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, which authority or body would have been responsible for determining that subsequent request?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Defence Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I move that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What does it show, Mr. Robson? Can you have the witness explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, are you able to explain what's going on, what this document describes?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The article we referred to earlier governs that the Defence Secretariat had the ongoing duty to examine the possible uses and the condition in which the requisitioned facilities were. It also had the duty to oversee whether the facilities were put to use as had originally been intended. In this particular instances he went out into the ground to examine precisely this. All these organs had to establish whether the facilities had indeed been requisitioned and whether it was being used as intended. It had to carry out its duty -- this duty as will all the other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Mr. Robson, we need from the witness an explanation as to then who requisitioned the Vatrostalna facility for the EMD, and what is the significance of the inspection which showed that, in fact, the El Mujahid Detachment was using the facilities properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, can you tell us who was it that requisitioned the Vatrostalna facility for the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that it was requisitioned by those who requested it and I presume that this unit submitted this request or some other unit that had previously been stationed there. It any case, the Municipal Defence Secretariat was the competent body to ensure that the facility is requisitioned for their purposes and to oversee whether the requisitioned facility was indeed being used for the purposes initially cited, in order to avoid the abuse of such facilities. Some instances of abuse had been reported elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So I'm sorry, but I need to understand why we're doing this. I sit with the picture that the El Mujahid Detachment requested the acquisition of this building. Now, for some reason the requisition was never formally filed but nevertheless the El Mujahedin then took over the building and subsequently this municipal body came to inspect the facilities to see if everything was all right. They came, and they were able to see that, yes, the facility was being used for the purpose for which it was requested, and so they left. This, if anything, shows that things were all right. They were working by the rules, and there was just this little mistake that a formal requisition was never filed. Is that what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point is and I'll put this as a question to the witness, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's your witness Mr. Robson and your document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Hubo, you have explained the procedure for assigning resources, including facilities, and we've discussed the El Mujahedin Detachment. Was the competent body, the Municipal Defence Secretariat, that determined these issues, a military body or a civilian body?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN HUBO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal organ decided whether to mobilize whether there was such need or not. Not the military organ. The military organ sent requests for that. In this particular instance, the Vatrostalna facility, in my view, had been requisitioned by some other military unit earlier on, and probably it remained requisitioned once the unit left. I believe that it had the status of having been requisitioned since 1992, and this municipal organ merely established that the facility had indeed been requisitioned whereas this other part, this other facility that had been used had not been formally requisitioned; and therefore it speaks of this subsequent request and the need to submit it in order for the facility to be formally requisitioned. Perhaps this is confusing. But can you see there is the 17th of June, 1995 and a great many things happened since 1992 I believe that the facility had been requisitioned as early as 1992, but I can't tell you this with precision because I don't have records. I suppose that when the unit took up this facility it was merely the user of the facility that changed but the status of the facility remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if this answer is understandable. If I may just put in a word or two concerning interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which answer, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Before my learned colleague does this, Your Honour, I just want to make sure that the way this is put to the witness is not done in a way that might suggest the answer or suggest another answer that Madam Vidovic might believe that he meant or that he said instead. I don't know if it would be appropriate if we're going to talk about interpretation and if Madam Vidovic is to say this is actually what he said when this is it what the interpretation was, it might be appropriate for the witness not to be present for that, Your Honour, so that we don't suggest any answers to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, are you talking about a misinterpretation on the transcript, because if you are then we can just ask the witness to repeat himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I refer to interpretation. I'm speaking in terms of what the witness says and what is reflected on the transcript. I didn't give any sort of explanation that could give even the remote intimation of me trying to give a suggestion to the witness, and let me sate this, since this the second time my learned friends have said that I wished to suggest something, and the truth couldn't be further than that. I wish to state that we have been having problems with interpretation all this time, and what I shall be asking in the future, Your Honours, is to have the tape of what the witness said played in the courtroom so that my learned friends would fully be aware of me wishing to merely point to misinterpretation rather than wishing to make any suggestions. I shall ask right after this hearing to be given a tape; and I will react in writing to every inconsistency in interpretation, and I will ask for the interpretation to be corrected. In order to avoid prolonging the testimony of this witness. However, Your Honours, I really resent being told that I am suggesting anything to the witness whenever I want to raise an interpretation issue. This is our right. It is my right to raise such an issue if what the witness has been saying is not correctly reflected in the transcript. I do not wish to be reproached in this manner, that's why I will ask for the tape to be checked after the hearing or for the tape to be checked during the hearing. I really don't think that I deserve such comments as we have been hearing from my learned friends from the Prosecution. Thank you very much for that Madam Vidovic. I want to suggest that the shortest, surest, and quickest way of correcting any misinterpretation issues is just to ask the witness to repeat the answer, and if the answer is still misinterpreted let us point out where the misinterpretation is and let's ask the witness to repeat that portion again and ask the interpreters to listen properly. I think that will be a quicker way and we will finish this trial much quicker that way. Mr. Hubo, Madam Vidovic suggests that the answer you gave at page 44, starting from line 3 to line 16, there is a misinterpretation somewhere. I would like to you repeat that answer. I realise it is a very long answer, unfortunately. If you want to be reminded of what you said in that answer, I can read to you what is said in that paragraph and then you can tell us whether it interprets you correctly. The question had been: -- I beg your pardon. The answer starts from line 25 of page 43.
